model.note: The weights are not in the repository. They are in the fsp-st archive of the release.
model.optimizer: Adam in the eigenbasis of each weight matrix's gradient moments, refreshed every 50 updates, the matrices of three-dimensional weights turned as well
model.training_windows: 512 bytes in batches of 8 up to 24,000 updates, then unbroken streams: 15 groups of 10 windows of 2,048 bytes that continue each other, in batches of 2, with a read reach of 2,048 cells; 4,096 targets an update throughout
model.schedule: 1,000 warmup updates, then cosine decay over the 90,000 updates

forked_at.from: fsp-st-p, v15's recipe with --read-forget on windows of 512 bytes, at the same peak rate and schedule

architecture.stack: eleven levels, each a state read of 8 heads and then a layer of 1,188 threshold cells, both writing their spikes back into one stream of 512 channels
architecture.forgetting: every read head learns a slope: a cell beyond the window takes the oldest age's offset plus the slope times the doublings of its age beyond the window
architecture.knowledge_cells: 128 learned cells a head that race beside the stream's own cells and never age

model.paths_note: The released file is the scored file with the training arguments that name folders rewritten to repository paths; its weights are identical.

spiking-byte-lm-v19-checkpoints-fsp-tf.t.what: the pair's Transformer: 11 blocks of width 512 with 8 heads and gated units, windows of 512 bytes for 24,000 updates and then of 2,048 bytes for 66,000, at its best full-size peak rate, 1.2e-3

spiking-byte-lm-v19-checkpoints-fs-loop6.what: the full-size looped stack of the loop pilot: levels 2 to 8 run twice with the same synapses, the pulse budget scaled with the passes to 507,000, 24,000 updates at peak rate 6e-4

spiking-byte-lm-v19-bits.tar.gz.what: per-piece bits and scoring records of every scoring in this release, under results/event_lm/knowledge_gap/bits: full_size_pair (the pair), full_size_pilots (the loop pilot and its budget control, the unit screen's third arm, the lifted gate, and the arms and bases of full_size_spikes_late), test_bed (the loop, skip-fibre and slope screens, server and laptop seeds) and plain_units (the float unit diagnostic)
